About the performance data

All notes and tempo changes are read from MIDI, and sound, fingertips and keys are synchronized to a single audio clock. Finger segments and arm lengths are fixed; the relaxed, hanging idle fingers, the striking finger's press, thumb crossings and wrist travel are drawn as continuous motion. The thumb base sits on the side of the palm near the wrist, and wrist flexion and arm lift follow the strength of each keystroke. In fast shifts the fingers spread ahead of the next figure, and the head nod, gaze and torso weight shift follow the phrasing. “Hands” keeps the pianist's own left–right orientation; “Pianist” frames the head and torso. The keyboard uses the proportions of 148 mm white keys and 95 mm black keys. Chords wider than one hand can reach are rolled, shifting sound and keystroke together. Fingering is chosen from the surrounding figures, reflecting scale fingerings, black/white key layout, chord span and finger changes for fast repeated notes. Notes within one hand position are joined while holding the palm in place, and in thumb crossings the hand moves between release and the next strike. “R”/“L” and 1–5 under the score show the chosen finger. Fingering and body motion are generated automatically and do not reproduce any real pianist. The damper (right) pedal follows MIDI CC64, sustaining and decaying released notes and moving the right foot and pedal; “Pedal” shows a close-up. The tone is a recorded Steinway grand: four recorded dynamic layers are blended smoothly, with pedal resonance, subtle reverb and quiet key and pedal noises. The score is an automatic transcription from MIDI pitch and tempo; short notes are beamed by beat and sounding noteheads are shown in gold. Voicing, rests and enharmonic spelling are not those of the original score.
